Try a script on the synthetic copy

trial_run.Rd

Runs the researcher's script on the copy from mimic() in a fresh, isolated R session and reports whether it runs through, which packages it uses, which files it writes, and whether it tries to save data at row level. Run it before sending a script for real_run(): a script that fails here will fail on the real data too, and a script that saves rows will be stopped at output checking.

Usage

trial_run(
  script,
  fake_data,
  output_dir = NULL,
  timeout = 600,
  config = NULL,
  check_output = TRUE
)

Arguments

script

Path to an R script, or R code as text.

fake_data

The synthetic copy: a data frame or a named list of data frames, normally from mimic().

output_dir

Directory the script writes to. By default a new temporary directory, returned in the result so the output can be looked at.

timeout

Maximum run time in seconds.

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the defaults. The output check uses the same rules, so give the configuration staff use. The script's safe_count(), safe_summary() and safe_model() follow it too.

check_output

Run the written files through inspect(); see the section above.

Value

An object of class mimic_trial with status ("ok", "warn" or "error"), error (message and script line), packages, files, writes, row_level (findings), inspection (the inspect() result for the written files, or NULL), warnings, log (the console output) and output_dir. A file that needs changes at the output check makes the status "warn".

How the script sees the data

Each table is available as an object named after it (persons, contacts, ...); a single data frame is called data. The working directory is the output directory, also available as output_dir. Write all output there with relative paths, exactly as on the real run.

How row-level output is detected

  • a write call (write.csv(), saveRDS(), fwrite(), ...) receives a table with many rows: at least 100 and at least half the rows of the smallest input table,

  • a written file contains identifier values from the copy. Text files, .rds and .RData files are searched; other formats are listed as not scanned.

The output check in advance

With check_output = TRUE the files the script writes are also run through inspect(), as staff will do with the output from the real run. The researcher sees from outside that a table shows a minimum, keeps a cell that is not suppressed or saves a model with everyone's residuals, and can fix the script before a run on the real data is spent on it.

The check reads only the output, not the copy: the rules that compare with the microdata (dominance, values held by few persons) need the real data and are left for inspect() inside. The counts come from the copy, so a cell can be small here and large in the real data, or the other way round. The mess mimic() adds (odd codes such as "?" and "999", empty strings) gives small cells in a table that tabulates the raw variable; that is a hint to clean the codes in the script, and a copy made with mess = FALSE shows whether anything else is wrong. A file that needs changes because of how it is built (a minimum column, a model object, a suppressed cell the totals give back) will need changes inside too; a file approved here is not yet approved.

Examples

# \donttest{
m <- profile_data(list(persons = fake_persons, contacts = fake_contacts),
                  keys = "person_id",
                  config = mimic_config(geo_vars = "settlement", text_vars = "note"))
copy <- mimic(m, seed = 1)
fit <- trial_run(c(
  "tab <- table(persons$sex)",
  "write.csv(as.data.frame(tab), 'sex.csv')"
), copy)
fit
#> <mimic_trial> (code)
#> ✔ The script ran through in 0 seconds.
#> ℹ Files written to C:/Users/danie/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpCclG4q/trial_run_7b841d6b2da0: sex.csv
#> ✖ Output check on the copy: 1 file would be sent back:
#> sex.csv
#> • 5 of 10 cells have fewer than 5 persons.
#> ℹ The copy has made-up mess (odd codes, empty strings): small cells may come from it. Clean the codes in the script, or try a copy made with `mimic(mess = FALSE)`.
#> See `$inspection` for every check.
# }
